Explain what overfitting is and why it is problematic.

set.modelAnswer: Overfitting happens when a model memorises the training examples, including their noise, instead of learning the general pattern. It then does very well on the training data but badly on new data, which is what matters in practice. A large gap between training and validation performance is a sign of it. It can be reduced with more training data, a simpler model, early stopping or regularisation.
keyPoints: The model memorises training examples, including noise
It does very well on training data but badly on new data
A large gap between training and validation performance is a sign
Remedies: more data, a simpler model, early stopping, regularisation

machine-learning.prompt: Explain the difference between regression and classification tasks in supervised learning.

set.modelAnswer: Both are supervised learning tasks that learn from labelled examples. Regression predicts a number, such as a price, while classification predicts a category, such as whether an email is spam.
keyPoints: Regression predicts a number
Classification predicts a category
Both are supervised learning with labelled examples
